definition: a sheet or thickness of a material that covers a surface or lies between other things

collocations.example: A thin layer of dust covered the office shelves.
The outer layer of the fruit protects the soft seeds.

definition: a hole or crack that lets liquid or gas escape by accident

collocations.example: A gas leak forced everyone to leave the building.
The mechanic quickly found the oil leak under the car.

definition: a legal contract to rent land or property for a set time

collocations.example: They signed a lease agreement for the new office space.
The lease term runs for five years from January.

definition: a strong material made from treated animal skin

collocations.example: The handbag is made from genuine leather.
He wore a black leather jacket to the meeting.

definition: a formal talk given to teach people about a subject

collocations.example: The professor will give a lecture on modern art.
Hundreds of students attended the lecture on economics.

definition: an old, popular story that may not be true

collocations.example: The haunted house story is just an urban legend.
An ancient legend tells of a dragon in the lake.

definition: to make or pass a new law

collocations.example: The government plans to legislate against unfair hiring.
Parliament will legislate on data privacy next year.

definition: allowed by and obeying the law

collocations.example: They run a legitimate business that pays all its taxes.
She earns a legitimate income from her shop.

definition: legally responsible for something

collocations.example: You are liable for any damage to the rented car.
The company was held liable for the accident.

definition: willing to accept different opinions and new ideas

collocations.example: She has a liberal attitude toward other cultures.
His liberal views on education surprised many colleagues.

definition: to free someone or something from control or captivity

collocations.example: Troops arrived to liberate the city from occupation.
The soldiers moved in to liberate the prisoners.

definition: the freedom to act, speak, or think as one wants

collocations.example: The new law protects each citizen's personal liberty.
The constitution guarantees religious liberty for all.

definition: a connection between two things or people

collocations.example: Poor training is the weak link in the whole system.
There is a close link between diet and good health.

definition: a substance that flows freely, like water

collocations.example: Pour the clear liquid into a clean glass.
The syrup is a thick liquid that pours slowly.

definition: following the exact and basic meaning of the words

collocations.example: The literal meaning of the phrase is quite different.
A literal translation often sounds unnatural in English.

definition: relating to books and serious writing

collocations.example: Her latest literary work received wide praise.
He teaches a course on modern literary criticism.

definition: written works valued as art, such as novels and poems

collocations.example: She studied classical literature at university.
The course covers great works of world literature.

definition: a large entrance area inside a public building

collocations.example: Guests waited for their taxi in the hotel lobby.
The visitors gathered in the main lobby downstairs.

definition: to formally present a complaint or claim to authorities

collocations.example: She decided to lodge a complaint with the manager.
You can lodge a claim for the damaged goods.

definition: a sensible way of thinking that follows clear reasons

collocations.example: Her argument was based on sound logic.
He explained the whole plan with clear logic.

definition: firmly supporting a person, group, or cause

collocations.example: The store rewards every loyal customer with discounts.
He remained a loyal supporter of the team for years.

definition: great comfort and pleasure from expensive things

collocations.example: They spent their honeymoon in a luxury hotel.
Sales of luxury goods rose sharply this year.

definition: a piece of metal that attracts iron and steel

collocations.example: The teacher used a bar magnet to show the field.
The small motor contains a permanent magnet.

definition: the larger number or part of a group

collocations.example: The vast majority of staff supported the change.
The motion finally passed by a narrow majority.

definition: to show or appear clearly

collocations.example: The disease can manifest itself in many ways.
His anger manifested in sharp, short replies.

definition: to handle or control something with skill

collocations.example: Researchers can manipulate data to test their ideas.
The pilot learned to manipulate the controls smoothly.

definition: a book that explains how to use or do something

collocations.example: Read the user manual before setting up the printer.
The engineer kept the reference manual on her desk.

definition: to make goods in large numbers, usually in a factory

collocations.example: The company manufactures goods for export worldwide.
They manufacture equipment used in modern hospitals.

definition: the amount by which one thing is greater or smaller than another

collocations.example: The team won the game by a narrow margin.
She passed the exam by a wide margin.

definition: relating to the sea and its plants and animals

collocations.example: Oil spills badly harm the marine environment.
Plastic waste is a major cause of marine pollution.

definition: behaving in a sensible, adult way

collocations.example: He has grown into a responsible, mature adult.
She is emotionally mature for someone so young.

definition: the elected leader of a city or town government

collocations.example: The deputy mayor opened the new library today.
The city will elect a new mayor next month.

definition: during the time between two events, or at the same time

collocations.example: The manager was away; meanwhile, the team kept working.
The bus is late; in the meantime, let's wait inside.

definition: a person whose job is to repair machines and engines

collocations.example: The car mechanic replaced the worn brakes.
A skilled mechanic can fix the engine quickly.

definition: a system or method for achieving a particular result

collocations.example: The bank set up a control mechanism for risky loans.
The company built an incentive mechanism to boost sales.

definition: the organizations that provide news to the public

collocations.example: The mass media shape how people see events.
The scandal received heavy media coverage.

definition: a method or means used to express or spread something

collocations.example: Television is a powerful medium for advertising.
Email is an effective medium for quick updates.

definition: a list of the food available at a restaurant

collocations.example: The restaurant offers a set menu for large groups.
The cafe changes its lunch menu every week.

definition: nothing more than what is stated; only

collocations.example: The final interview was a mere formality.
Their meeting was a mere coincidence, nothing more.

definition: to join together to form one thing

collocations.example: The small bank will merge with a larger rival.
The two lanes merge into one near the bridge.

definition: a planned way of doing something

collocations.example: The new teaching method improved students' scores.
They explained the research method in detail.

definition: to move from one place or region to another

collocations.example: Many birds migrate south before winter arrives.
These animals migrate seasonally to find food.

definition: not strong, severe, or extreme

collocations.example: The island enjoys a mild climate all year.
She had only a mild form of the illness.

definition: a person whose job is to dig coal or metal from the ground

collocations.example: His grandfather worked as a coal miner for decades.
The gold miner searched the river for tiny flakes.

definition: the smallest amount or level that is possible or allowed

collocations.example: Many of the workers earn only the minimum wage.
A degree is the minimum requirement for this job.

definition: a government department responsible for an area of work

collocations.example: She works for a large government ministry.
The foreign ministry issued a statement today.

definition: a flying weapon that is aimed at a distant target

collocations.example: The ship fired a guided missile at the target.
The cruise missile flew low over the water.

definition: a combination of different things mixed together

collocations.example: The dish was a strange mixture of sweet and sour.
Her perfume was a rich mixture of flowers and spice.

definition: able to be moved or carried easily

collocations.example: She answered her mobile phone during lunch.
You can read the report on any mobile device.

definition: a particular way of doing or operating something

collocations.example: The train is my favorite mode of transport.
The machine has a quiet mode of operation.

definition: medium in amount or degree; not extreme

collocations.example: They sell good coffee at a moderate price.
The region has a moderate climate with mild winters.

definition: fairly small in size, amount, or value

collocations.example: They live comfortably on a modest income.
The company reported a modest increase in sales.

definition: to make small changes to something

collocations.example: Engineers had to modify the design for safety.
The reward system helped modify the children's behavior.

definition: a separate unit that is part of a larger system

collocations.example: The new software module handles customer payments.
The control module manages the entire system.

definition: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its properties

collocations.example: A water molecule contains hydrogen and oxygen.
The drug is based on a simple small molecule.

definition: to watch and check something over a period of time

collocations.example: Teachers monitor each student's progress carefully.
Doctors will closely monitor her recovery.

definition: a large, frightening imaginary creature

collocations.example: Sailors told stories of a huge sea monster.
The child drew a scary monster with sharp teeth.

definition: relating to what is right and wrong in behavior

collocations.example: She felt a moral obligation to help the poor.
He refused to lie because of his moral principles.

definition: in addition to what has already been said

collocations.example: The costs are high. Moreover, the plan may not work.
The site is small; moreover, it is far from the station.

definition: causing death or likely to cause death

collocations.example: The climbers were in mortal danger during the storm.
The soldier suffered a mortal wound in battle.

definition: a loan from a bank used to buy a house or property

collocations.example: They took out a home mortgage to buy the house.
Their monthly mortgage payment rose sharply this year.

definition: the act or process of moving

collocations.example: The replay showed the goal in slow motion.
The dancer lifted her arm in one smooth motion.

definition: a reason that makes someone do something

collocations.example: I think he has an ulterior motive for helping us.
The decision was driven purely by the profit motive.

definition: many; involving several people or things

collocations.example: The reporter checked the story with multiple sources.
He called her multiple times during the day.

definition: a building where interesting objects are shown to the public

collocations.example: They spent the afternoon at the art museum.
The science museum has a new space exhibit.

definition: shared or felt equally by two or more people

collocations.example: A good partnership is built on mutual trust.
The deal was signed for the mutual benefit of both firms.

definition: a widely believed idea that is not actually true

collocations.example: It is a common myth that we use only part of our brain.
The article aims to dispel a popular health myth.

definition: not covered, hidden, or protected

collocations.example: The tiny insect is hard to see with the naked eye.
Keep the gas cylinder away from any naked flame.

definition: to tell a story or describe events in order

collocations.example: The grandmother loves to narrate a bedtime story.
The witness began to narrate the events of that night.

definition: bad or harmful; not hopeful or helpful

collocations.example: Too much screen time has a negative effect on sleep.
His negative attitude discouraged the whole team.

definition: to fail to give proper care or attention to something

collocations.example: He was fired for neglecting his duties at work.
Working too hard, she began to neglect her health.

definition: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement

collocations.example: The two sides met to negotiate a new deal.
Her lawyer helped negotiate the contract terms.

definition: a material made of crossed threads with holes between them

collocations.example: The crew pulled the heavy fishing net onto the deck.
Her shot clipped the top of the tennis net.

definition: a large system of connected people, things, or places

collocations.example: The office shares files over a computer network.
The company built a wide distribution network.

definition: not supporting any side in a disagreement or conflict

collocations.example: The country chose to remain neutral during the war.
The referee must keep a neutral position in disputes.

definition: in spite of what has just been said; even so

collocations.example: The task was very hard. Nevertheless, the team finished on time.
He was tired; nevertheless, he finished the whole report.

definition: to move your head up and down to show agreement

collocations.example: The students nodded in agreement with the teacher.
She nodded her head to show she understood.

definition: to formally suggest someone for a position or prize

collocations.example: They decided to nominate her for the service award.
Each party will nominate a candidate for the election.

definition: an idea or belief about something

collocations.example: He had only a vague notion of how engines work.
She gave up her romantic notion of city life.

definition: a long written story about imaginary people and events

collocations.example: She wrote a historical novel set in ancient Rome.
The gothic novel is full of dark, spooky scenes.

definition: relating to the energy released from atoms

collocations.example: The country gets much of its electricity from nuclear power.
The treaty aims to reduce the number of nuclear weapons.

definition: existing in large numbers; many

collocations.example: He has visited Japan on numerous occasions.
The report gives numerous examples of the problem.

definition: to express disagreement with or opposition to something

collocations.example: Several staff objected to the new schedule.
Residents strongly object to the building plan.

definition: a goal or aim that you are trying to achieve

collocations.example: The main objective is to cut costs this year.
Growth in Asia is a key strategic objective.

definition: to make someone do something because of a law or duty

collocations.example: The rules oblige drivers to wear a seat belt.
The contract legally obliges them to pay on time.

definition: to get something, often by effort or request

collocations.example: Reporters work hard to obtain accurate information.
The police need a warrant to obtain evidence.

definition: a person's job or main activity

collocations.example: Firefighting is a dangerous occupation that demands great courage.
Farming is the main occupation in that region.

definition: to fill or take up an amount of space or time

collocations.example: The large desk occupies most of the small office.
Reading helps occupy my time on long flights.

definition: a very large area of sea

collocations.example: Strange creatures live in the deep ocean.
Scientists mapped a new part of the ocean floor.

definition: an illegal act; a crime

collocations.example: Driving without a license is a criminal offense.
He paid a fine for a minor traffic offense.

definition: to make someone feel upset or angry

collocations.example: The joke might offend some people in the room.
His rude remarks deeply offended the guests.

definition: a play in which the words are sung to music

collocations.example: The new opera house seats two thousand people.
They enjoyed a light comic opera on Friday night.

definition: a person who competes against or disagrees with another

collocations.example: She faced a strong opponent in the final match.
The senator debated his political opponent on television.

definition: spoken rather than written

collocations.example: Students take an oral exam to test their speaking.
She gave a clear oral presentation to the class.

definition: a part of the body that does a particular job

collocations.example: He is waiting for an organ transplant at the hospital.
The eye is an important sense organ.

definition: grown or produced without artificial chemicals

collocations.example: She prefers to buy organic food at the market.
Organic farming avoids artificial chemicals and sprays.

definition: focused toward or mainly concerned with something

collocations.example: A good editor must be detail-oriented and careful.
The firm is highly customer-oriented in its service.

definition: the point or place where something begins

collocations.example: The label shows the product's country of origin.
The survey asked about each person's ethnic origin.

definition: the final result of an action or process

collocations.example: The team discussed every possible outcome of the plan.
A fair deal is the most likely outcome of the talks.
